nodes.title: Cycle 1 · Initiating Epistemological Inquiry on Belief Justification

detail.title: Initiating Epistemological Inquiry on Belief Justification
detail.summary: This cycle begins a project focused on the epistemology of belief justification under conditions of uncertainty and noisy evidence. We are prioritizing the current attention directive by launching a project to explore how distinct philosophical frameworks—such as Bayesianism, Reliabilism, and Evidentialism—address the challenges of forming justified beliefs when data is filtered through imperfect observers or incomplete information.

detail.next_step: Search for academic overviews of epistemic justification theories regarding uncertainty.
detail.question: How do different epistemological frameworks account for belief justification when evidence is noisy or partial?
detail.reason: To establish a foundational framework for analyzing how beliefs are formed and justified in non-ideal conditions.
detail.title: Justification Under Uncertainty

nodes.title: epistemic justification theories bayesianism reliabilism evidentialism uncertainty

detail.query: epistemic justification theories bayesianism reliabilism evidentialism uncertainty
detail.reason: To identify key theories and academic literature that address belief justification when evidence is incomplete or unreliable.
